html:
The Rwandan Revolution was the overthrow of the Tutsi monarchy and chiefs by the Hutu majority between 1959 and 1961, which ended with independence on 1 July 1962.

It began in November 1959, when an attack on a Hutu leader set off attacks on Tutsi homes across the country. Belgian officials replaced Tutsi chiefs with Hutu. Parties led by Grégoire Kayibanda won elections, the monarchy was abolished by referendum in 1961, and the country became independent as a republic.

Many thousands of Tutsi were killed in these years, and over a hundred thousand fled to Uganda, Burundi and Congo. Their children formed the Rwandan Patriotic Front, which invaded in 1990. The revolution ended the Belgian order but kept its idea of race.
sum: The Rwandan Revolution was the overthrow of the Tutsi monarchy and chiefs by the Hutu majority between 1959 and 1961, which ended with independence on 1 July 1962.
